Few days ago I migrated my OpenClaw agent to an empty VPS, it was a bare server with just Nova and OpenCode running on it.

Then I added Nova to a group chat and changed the bot's settings to allow others to talk to it. Sure enough they did, near a thousand messages were exchanged with my bot. Most of it was an attempt at hacking or breaking the system.

Then at the end of the day I gave Nova the command to ignore everyone when I slept. Sure enough it did.

But

somehow cleverly chained multiple prompts together, bypassing my command to Nova to ignore others, making it context overload and finally gaining access to Nova, which also then gave access to the insecure server.

It was actually impressive (😭) and he wrote a good autopsy of the whole interaction. If you've got an OpenClaw agent it's worth a read!

Now round 2 will commence when I actually secure and set things up properly and they'll try to hack it again.

posts.title: Loved this! 🥲
segments:
Loved this! 🥲

If i ever had a cafe, i would have a broke-accino on my menu ... that's a cappuccino but its also coffee and milk, and its also from yesterday, and its also good with cheap cigarettes on the side. but the broke writer who always sits in the corner doesn't mind, he just wants to be in the space, and he wants to be there all the time, preferably with something warm between his hands, he has called it home, and i cant find myself to evict him. he comes before we wipe the tables so when he leaves there are dust marks the exact size of his laptop, his hands, his phone, his journal and even dust marks of his perfect tiny butt still resides on the chair. i would often go to him with his order already in my hands, and he'd lasso me into his world with his sharp tongue and his slow gestures. he doesn't look me in the eye too often but when he does, i wouldn't be able to leave. i'd move into the tiny home he has made with his thoughts in the quite shaded corner of my little cafe, preferably with a broke-acciono also in my hands. some people pay with presence more than they can ever pay in monetary value. thats the price of my broke-accino, your presence.
